title: Chirurgie des surfaces conformes : notes manuscrites (s.d., 1983-1984), lettres (1984).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues a case-by-case search for a canonical Riemannian metric attached to a conformal surface X of the simplest types (plane, punctured plane, torus, RP^2, sphere). It belongs to the 'chirurgie des surfaces conformes' project, where such normalised metrics are presumably needed on the standard building blocks.

(2°, end) X ≅ E_C, a complex torus. The universal cover gives X a canonical structure of complex affine line, i.e. a translation structure (the NB). The flat Riemannian metrics compatible with the conformal structure and invariant under translations exist. They form one orbit under rescaling by u ∈ R^{+*}, so they are unique up to a positive constant. They are characterised by translation invariance and depend only on the underlying conformal structure. This is the standard fact that a conformal torus carries a unique flat conformal metric up to scale, which can be normalised by area 1.

(3) X ≅ real projective plane with a conformal structure. The orientation double cover X^or is P^1(C) with a fixed-point-free antiholomorphic involution σ (the 'antipodisme'). Among the round, Fubini–Study type metrics compatible with the conformal structure, there is presumably exactly one invariant under σ once the area is normalised to 1. Reason: the centraliser of σ in PGL_2(C) is the compact group SO(3), whose invariant hermitian form is unique up to scale. Since this metric is σ-invariant it descends to X, giving a canonical spherical metric of area 1 on any conformal RP^2.

(3') X ≅ P^1_C. One looks for metrics invariant under the automorphisms, but Aut = PGL_2(C) is non-compact, so there is no canonical metric. The next page repairs this by choosing a compact subgroup H of Aut_conf(X), lifting H^+ to SU-type subgroups of SL(V), and using an invariant hermitian form.
errors: No real mathematical error on this page. The phrase rendered 'une classe de telles est transitive par u∈R^{+*}' should mean that the translation-invariant flat metrics form a single R^{+*}-orbit; it is a statement about uniqueness up to scale, not transitivity of an action on X.

The uniqueness of the compatible spherical metric in case 3 depends on σ-invariance; the conformal structure on P^1 alone admits a whole PSL_2(C)/PSU_2 = H^3 family of such metrics. The text is garbled here but the intended meaning seems correct.

ideas.what: A conformal torus has a canonical complex affine (translation) structure and a flat compatible metric unique up to positive scale, determined by translation invariance
ideas.modern_name: Flat metric in the conformal class of a torus (uniformization)

ideas.what: Conformal RP^2: lift to P^1 with a fixed-point-free antiholomorphic involution; the unique invariant round metric of area 1 descends
ideas.modern_name: Uniformization of non-orientable surfaces via orientation double cover; uniqueness of conformal structure on RP^2

ideas.what: On P^1_C no canonical metric exists because the conformal automorphism group is non-compact (continued on the next page with a compact subgroup H)
ideas.modern_name: Round metrics on S^2 parametrised by PSL_2(C)/PSU(2) = hyperbolic 3-space

deep.surprise_reason: Standard uniformization facts worked out as a case list of canonical normalised metrics for the 'chirurgie des surfaces conformes' project. Nothing here is new to specialists.
transcription_corrections: NB likely reads: 'X est canoniquement munie d'une structure de droite affine sur C'.
Case 3 heading: the crossed-out words precede 'X ≃ plan projectif réel'. 'Dans ce cas' — the word struck out before 'cas' is not 'premier' with certainty.
'on [?] a qu'il revient au [?] =' plausibly reads 'on voit qu'il existe une, et une seule, métrique "euclidienne sphérique" compatible avec la structure conforme'.
Bracket likely: '[Celle-ci supposée normalisée par la condition que l'aire de la surface soit =1]'.
'une classe de telles est transitive par u∈R^{+*}' is uncertain; the intended sense is that such metrics are determined up to a factor u ∈ R^{+*}.
The last line of 3') is uncertain, roughly: 'par les automorphismes — dans ce cas structure conforme ... sur X'.
